home.title: Got a letter from HMRC? Understand it. Sort it.
home.intro: Upload a photo or PDF. We explain it in plain English or Romanian, show your deadlines, and help you appeal a penalty if you had a good reason.
home.how_1: Upload your letter. We read it and explain what it means and when your deadlines are.
home.how_2: Got a penalty? Answer a few questions. We tell you honestly whether HMRC is likely to accept your reason.
home.how_3: If you can appeal, get the official form filled in, in English, ready to sign and send.
home.o1_text: Plain-language explanation, key dates and next steps.
home.o2_text: Appeal form filled in from your answers and emailed to you. You sign and post it.
home.o3_text: A qualified accountant checks and improves your appeal within 48 hours.
home.pay_note: You only pay once we've checked an appeal is possible.

upload.title: Upload your letter
upload.intro: Take a photo of each page, or choose a PDF or image.
upload.limits: PDF, JPG or PNG · up to 10 MB · include every page
upload.tips: Lay the letter flat in good light, with all four corners in the picture. Make sure the date and reference numbers are readable.
upload.consent: I agree that Tax Letter Sorted can read this letter to explain it. It's deleted automatically after 24 hours unless I buy an appeal.
upload.error_unreadable: We couldn't read this letter clearly. Please try a clearer photo or the PDF.
upload.error_too_big: This file is over 10 MB. Please choose a smaller file.
upload.error_not_recognised: We don't recognise this type of letter yet. A qualified accountant can look at it for you.
upload.consent_needed: Please tick the box to continue.
upload.error_type: This type of file isn't supported. Please use PDF, JPG or PNG.
upload.error_too_many: You can add up to 10 pages per letter.
upload.error_generic: Something went wrong. Please try again in a moment.
upload.preview_received: Test upload received safely. Case reference: {ref}. Reading the letter is the next part being built.

check.penalty_may_be_wrong: This penalty may have been charged by mistake. An accountant should check it before you pay or appeal.
check.higher_12m_penalty: This penalty is higher than the usual amount. An accountant should look at it with you.

q.title: What happened?
q.intro: Answer in your own words, in any language. Only tell us what's true.
q.filed: Have you filed the return now?
q.not_filed_note: HMRC is expecting your tax return first. Filing it now stops further penalties.
q.file_first: File first: get help with my return
q.file_yourself: Or file it yourself on GOV.UK
q.reason: What stopped you filing on time?
q.reason_paying: What stopped you paying on time?
q.reasons_accepted: Reasons HMRC says it may accept
q.health_consent: I agree you can use what I tell you about my health only to prepare my appeal. It's deleted 14 days after my appeal is emailed.
q.problem_from_to: When did this start and end?
q.problem_at_deadline: Was this happening at, or shortly before, the deadline?
q.filed_as_soon_as_able: Did you file as soon as you could once it ended?
q.keep_evidence: Keep all your evidence. HMRC may ask for it to support your appeal.
q.why_late_note: HMRC accepts late appeals only if there was a good reason for the delay.
q.other_penalty_letters_same_year: Have you had other penalty letters for the same tax year?
q.more_than_one_year: Are your penalties for more than one tax year?
q.had_payment_plan: Did you have a payment plan with HMRC before this penalty?

warn.return_not_filed: HMRC usually won't decide your appeal until your return is filed. My appeal may be delayed or refused until then. I understand and want to continue.

reason.bereavement: Your partner or a close relative died shortly before the deadline
reason.hospital: An unexpected stay in hospital stopped you dealing with your tax
reason.computer_failure: Your computer or software failed while you were preparing your online return
reason.fire_flood_theft: A fire, flood or theft stopped you completing your return
reason.postal_delay: Postal delays you couldn't have predicted
reason.disability_mental_illness: Delays because of a disability or mental illness you have
reason.unaware_obligation: You didn't know about, or misunderstood, what you had to do
reason.relied_on_someone: You relied on someone else to send your return, and they didn't
reason.never_needed_to_file: I never needed to file a tax return

nnf.paye_only: Only employed, all tax paid through PAYE
nnf.under_trading_allowance: Self-employed income under the £1,000 trading allowance
nnf.stopped_before_year: Stopped self-employment before that tax year

nnf.hmrc_check_first: HMRC's own letter says: if you didn't need to send a tax return, tell HMRC using its free online checker. If HMRC agrees, it cancels the penalty. Try this first, before the 30-day appeal deadline.
nnf.appeal_instead: Prefer a formal appeal? Choose an option below.

na.online_too_hard: I found the online system too difficult
na.no_reminder: I didn't get a reminder from HMRC
na.mistake_on_return: I made a mistake on my return

option.file_return: File my tax return to stop further penalties

na.file_to_stop_more_penalties: If your return isn't filed yet, file it now to stop further penalties (daily penalties start after 3 months).

ne.text: You told us: {reason}. HMRC's guidance says this is not normally a reasonable excuse.

ne.change_answers_hint: If something else happened that you didn't mention, change your answers.
ne.not_sure_text: If your situation is more complicated, a qualified accountant can look at it with you.

talk.title: Talk to an accountant first
talk.text_choice: You told us: {reason}. HMRC accepts this reason less often, so a quick free call with an accountant can help you decide.
talk.text_callback: Your situation needs a closer look by an accountant before an appeal is prepared.
talk.consent: I agree Accounted4Tax can contact me about my penalty.
talk.retention: We keep your letter and answers until we've spoken, for no more than 30 days. Your appeal deadline is {date}.

callback.title: We'll call you
callback.text: Usually within one working day. After the call we'll email you a link to continue with your appeal, if that's right for you.

pay.title: Paying what you owe
pay.hours: Monday to Friday 8am to 8pm, Saturday 8am to 4pm

lp.contact_hmrc_about_plan: Contact HMRC to discuss this penalty, as you had a payment plan in place.

product.accountant_call_text: Talk your situation through with a qualified accountant. If you then choose Option 3, the £19 counts towards it.

help.title: Get help with your tax return
help.intro: A qualified accountant at Accounted4Tax can prepare and file your return. Leave your details and we'll call or email you, usually within one working day. No obligation.
help.consent: I agree Accounted4Tax can contact me about this request.
help.sent_text: A qualified accountant at Accounted4Tax will call or email you, usually within one working day.
help.wait_text: Have your HMRC letter, your UTR and any income records to hand. If your penalty has a deadline, it still applies.

confirm.title: Check your facts in English
confirm.intro: HMRC needs your appeal in English. Make sure the English says exactly what you told us. We haven't added anything.
confirm.declaration: These facts are true and complete. I understand a false statement to HMRC can lead to further penalties.

details.title: Your details
details.intro: HMRC needs these on the appeal form. We've filled in what we could read from your letter.
details.mobile_hint: Only used if there's a problem with your appeal.
details.agree_terms: I agree to the {terms} and have read the {privacy}.
details.waive_cancel: Send my appeal straight away. I understand I lose my 14-day right to cancel once it's delivered.
details.marketing: Optional: email me tax deadline reminders and tips from Accounted4Tax. Unsubscribe any time.
details.stripe_note: Next you'll see Stripe's secure payment page with your email already filled in. You only enter your card.

review.title: Review your appeal
review.intro: This is the official SA370 form, filled in from your confirmed answers.
review.form_in_english: The form is in English because it goes to HMRC.
review.sign_text: After you approve, we email you the form. Download it, print it, then sign and date it before posting.
review.confirm: I've read the form and it says what I want to tell HMRC.
review.approve: Approve and email it to me

done.title: Your appeal is ready
done.emailed: We've emailed it to {email}. If it isn't there in 5 minutes, check your spam folder.
done.print_sign: Download and print the form from the email, then sign and date it.
done.evidence_copies: Add copies of any evidence you have. Evidence helps HMRC decide. Never send originals. No evidence? Just send the form.
done.keep_copy: Keep a copy and a proof of postage.
done.privacy_note: Your private case link is in the email. For your privacy we delete your letter, answers and form on {date}, 14 days after sending.

o3.details_intro: Your accountant will use these to contact you about your appeal.
o3.name_as_id: Full name, as on your ID
o3.address_hint: Must match your proof of address.
o3.id_notice: After payment we'll ask for photo ID and proof of address. As an AAT-supervised practice, the law requires us to check who you are before we act for you.
o3.agree_terms: I agree to the {terms}, including the Option 3 engagement terms, and have read the {privacy}.
o3.start_now: Start the review now. If I cancel within 14 days, I'll pay for work already done.
o3.id_intro: Money laundering rules require us to confirm who you are before we act for you. It takes about 2 minutes.
o3.photo_id_hint: Passport, driving licence or national ID card
o3.proof_address_hint: Bank statement, utility bill or council tax bill from the last 3 months, showing your name and home address
o3.evidence_hint: Add your evidence so your accountant can check it.
o3.id_retention: We keep ID records for 5 years after our work for you ends, as the law requires. Only your accountant sees them.
o3.review_by: Eduard Husaru MAAT will review your appeal by {datetime}.
o3.next_2_text: We may email you a question. Please reply quickly so the deadline isn't missed.
o3.next_3_text: You get an email from iLovePDF with a link to sign. No account needed.
o3.next_4: Your appeal is posted to HMRC
o3.case_link_sent: We've emailed you a private link to follow your case.
o3.sign_within: Please sign within 2 days so we can post it in time.
o3.resend_link: We also emailed you the signing link. Can't find it?
o3.questions: Questions? Reply to any of our emails or call {phone}.
o3.signed_copy: A copy of your signed appeal is in your email.
o3.we_post: We'll post your appeal and evidence to HMRC by {date} and email you the proof of postage.
o3.after_text: HMRC will write to you, not to us, with its decision. This usually takes several weeks. You don't have to pay the penalty while the appeal is open.
o3.if_refused: If HMRC says no, contact us and we'll explain your options.
